translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Chopin’s cool, precise, ironic third person and her lyrical passages on the sea are rendered in natural, restrained Vietnamese; Edna’s awakening is neither moralised nor softened.
decisions.rationale: The novel’s force is in its restraint.

decisions.decision: French and Spanish words and sung lines are kept as printed, with the surrounding text giving the sense.
decisions.rationale: The Creole setting is part of the book’s sound.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Edna’s youngest sister Janet was called her elder sister (units 27, 46, 47 and 793) although she is the youngest; corrected.
The ‘like a dog’ idiom was misread (unit 72).
‘feverish’ was rendered as malarial chills (762), ‘knowing’ as ‘biết điều’ (663) and ‘told him it was plumb’ as ‘nói thẳng’ (776); corrected.
The narration called Edna ‘bà’ through unit 827 and ‘cô’ from unit 829 to the end with no source reason; ‘bà’ is now used throughout.
‘dinner’ (the midday meal in the source) was rendered ‘bữa tối’ in units 17, 28, 30 and 154; now ‘bữa chính’, with unit 173 matching.
Lexical slips and calques (for example ‘ngày kia’ for ‘on such a day’, ‘grotesque’ rendered four ways) were corrected.
Address forms between Edna, Adèle, Victor and Reisz were made consistent across all ranges.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: bà Pontellier / Edna; the pronoun in narration is ‘bà’
glossary.rationale: One form of reference for Edna in narration throughout the book; a first draft switched from ‘bà’ to ‘cô’ in the second half.

glossary.draft_rendering: Margaret = chị; Janet = em gái út
glossary.rationale: Janet is the youngest sister; a first draft had called her the elder.
Address forms fixed for the whole book after the first review.

glossary.source_term: French and Spanish words, sung lines
glossary.rationale: The parrot’s ‘Allez vous-en! Sapristi!’, ‘Ah! si tu savais’ and music titles stay in the original language as in the source.

witness_decision: Selected the novel The Awakening from Project Gutenberg #160, an electronic transcription of The Awakening and Selected Short Stories. The Gutenberg page does not name the printing; the text follows Kate Chopin’s 1899 novel (Chicago and New York: Herbert S. Stone) and was not collated with it.

unresolved_questions.explanation: A few phrases remain slightly literal, for example ‘tham vọng tự phụ’ at unit 575.

title_review.rationale: The Vietnamese title ‘Sự thức tỉnh’ is this edition’s own rendering; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening: the parrot in its cage on the porch.
The last paragraph: the sea and the hum of bees.
